title: BGN y-factor economy with a rare priced CRASH in the state y: a different distribution of shocks
question: Does a fat left tail in the priced state, with its own price, change the fair gap in BGN?
notes:
GROUP 1 (different distributions: crash) in BGN, which had no run in that cell (the disaster programme was declined before any run). bvych0's chain with its transition replaced by a mixture: with probability pj 0.01 a month the state jumps to its lowest node (-3.5 sd) instead of following the Tauchen transition, and the jump carries its own kernel factor exp(gj) with gj 2.0 (risk-neutral jump probability 7.4% a month before renormalisation), not the Gaussian price extrapolated to a fifteen-sd move. The same object as GS21's gvyp10j. Every firm type's exposure to the crash is its exposure to y.

PRE-CHECK (120-firm panel, 2026-10-12): type premia 8.5 / 10.1 / 13.2 %/yr (control 8.6 / 10.7 / 14.3), SR_max by y-tercile 0.32 / 0.39 / 0.45 (control 0.41 / 0.43 / 0.45): the crash lowers the attainable Sharpe in the low-y months. Euler equation on the chain exact to machine precision; DP residual 1e-7.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; id read from the Quest build log before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-12, before the run): the crash changes the level and timing of premia, not their shape in the ranks: room and fair gap within noise of bvych0's. FALSIFIED as 'the distribution of shocks matters for the gap' if the fair gap differs from bvych0's by more than +-0.010 on the same seeds in 7 of 10.
